significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that “per-step verification effort … decays monotonically with normalized chain position and anti-aligns with the fragility profile,” while a separable, causally effective “verification-engagement” signal mediates that mismatch: a form-(iii) positional law combined with a form-(ii) mechanism, rather than merely the standard direction-plus-steering template. The phenomenon would predict verification and failure profiles at unmeasured chain positions, while the mechanism would explain why targeted allocation can outperform uniform checking; this bears directly on the stepwise process supervision used in Lightman et al., “Let’s Verify Step by Step” (2023), and the allocation of inference computation studied by Snell et al., “Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters” (2024). The branches are determinate: absence of the gradient rules out the central positional-allocation explanation, while decay explained by difficulty supports rational allocation instead—although the claim incorrectly says that absence would falsify uniform verification, when it would instead be consistent with it. After topic substitution, generic mechanistic work on efficient reasoning would not earn this score; the specific anti-aligned monotonic profiles and their causal linkage are what place it materially above the topic median.

reach.justification: The claim names several concrete handles: the per-step “verification effort” profile, the residual-stream “verification-engagement” projection, “position-aware verifier placement,” and “adaptive decoding that spends verification where fragility is highest.” These are ex-ante handles because they can increase checking before a late step silently corrupts the answer, leaving an action window for inference systems and practitioners who gate or deploy reasoning agents rather than serving only post-hoc analysis. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation—engagement should decay monotonically with position and anti-align with fragility—although the particular steering direction itself may require rediscovery; the asserted scope extends across reasoning models and potentially “sequential deliberation,” but cross-architecture generality is phrased cautiously as “need not be specific to CoT prompting.” Topic substitution would leave only generic efficient-reasoning interventions and would not justify this score; the transferable positional relation, named adaptive-decoding rule, and practitioner-facing lead time support the higher band.
